21 minutes read

Continuous integration

This page is the CI design for this repository. It says which lane runs what, how long each lane may take, and which status check branch protection requires. The proposal is recorded in decision 0024. That record is proposed: these lanes become the standard when the maintainer accepts them. Later tasks in epic #1985 change workflows to match this page; until then, a workflow may still differ from the target below.

Scans in this repository stay offline. No CI lane adds network access to the scan engine.

Single required check

Branch protection and the merge queue require one status check: ci-ok.

ci-ok is a job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. It runs after the other jobs in that workflow, fails when any needed job failed or was cancelled, and passes when every needed job succeeded or was skipped. Keep individual jobs, the public corpus, Scorecard, fuzz, mutation, and package smoke out of the required list so the matrix can change without editing repository settings.

How to turn the check and the merge queue on: MAINTAINERS.md. Contributor-facing note: CONTRIBUTING.md.

Lanes at a glance

Lane Trigger Purpose Wall-clock budget Required to merge?
Pull request pull_request Fast feedback for authors 25 minutes No — informs review; ci-ok on the PR is useful but the queue is the landing proof
Merge queue merge_group Proof that may land on main 30 minutes Yes — ci-ok must pass; the run is never cancelled
Main push to main Post-merge side effects only (after the queue is the only path) 15 minutes N/A — already merged
Nightly schedule / workflow_dispatch Expensive, network, or slow signals 60 minutes per workflow No
Release tag / publish chain Verify, build, publish, smoke 45 minutes for the chain N/A — gated by the release checklist

A job's timeout-minutes must fit its lane. Raising a lane budget, or moving work between lanes, updates this page in the same change as the workflow edit.

Runner-minute budget (350)

Wall-clock time is not the only cost. A pull request also spends runner minutes: for each job, its timeout-minutes times the number of jobs its matrix expands to, summed over every workflow that can start on pull_request. The budget is 350 runner minutes: the 325-minute ceiling measured on 2026-11-04 plus the 25-minute mutation-pr.yml job that mutation-tests the changed lines (#2104). ci.yml is the largest part: four check shards at 20 minutes each, coverage, the Windows cross-OS run, docs, and the small jobs.

npm run check runs tools/check-workflow-change.ts, which recomputes the ceiling from the workflow files and fails above the budget. It is offline: it reads the workflows, git history, and the event payload file Actions already writes. A job without timeout-minutes is charged the 25-minute pull-request lane budget, so a new job cannot hide its cost. Matrix include entries and dynamic fromJSON dimensions count as one job, so the number is a ceiling rather than an estimate of a particular run.

When a pull request changes a workflow under .github/workflows/, it must also fill in the Workflow changes section of the pull request template: the reason, and the effect on this budget (for example +20 runner minutes, -5, or none). The check compares the stated effect with the measured change. A workflow change without the note fails, and a note that understates the effect fails too. The note is enforced on pull_request runs, where the body exists; the merge queue has no pull-request body and re-runs only the budget.

Raising the budget is a design change: update this page and PULL_REQUEST_RUNNER_MINUTE_BUDGET in the tool in the same pull request, and say why in the note. Do not raise it to make a single change pass.

Pull request (25 minutes)

Goal. Catch failures early without pretending the pull request is the landing proof.

Always (code changes).

  • Classify docs-only vs code (ci.yml changes job).
  • npm run check on Ubuntu with Node 24 and Node 22.
  • Run only the test files a change can reach, from an import map (tools/run-tests-selection.ts); the coverage job still measures the whole suite on every pull request. Shared paths, configuration, fixtures, the registry, and the map's own code run everything.
  • npm run check on Windows with Node 24 (path and line-ending bugs before merge).
  • Quality gate against origin/main, dependency audit, Action cold-start budget, generated docs and data checks, coverage floors and per-file coverage diff — on the Linux Node 24 job.
  • Dogfood the Action against this repository's baseline on that same job.
  • Pack the npm tarball on Linux and on the cross-OS runner and compare the hashes in ci-ok, so a build step that depends on the host — a path, a line ending, a file-ordering difference — fails before merge (record:reproducible, compare-build-hashes.mjs).
  • Decision-record presence when schemas/, src/sdk.ts, or src/mcp.ts change (decisions.yml).
  • Rule fixtures when they change or @velella/ebb moves to another version (rules.yml).
  • The runner-minute budget on every npm run check, plus the workflow-change note when .github/workflows/ changes (tools/check-workflow-change.ts).

Docs-only pull requests. Skip the test matrix. Build and check reference pages, verify llms-full.txt, dashboard/data.json, and api/v1 are buildable, generate llms-full.txt, sitemap.xml, rules/index.md, dashboard/data.json, and api/v1 for the Mizzen site, and build the site instead.

When site files change (docs/ site sources, theme config, and Lighthouse config).

  • Site budget, docs doctor, and related site checks, through the paths filters on those workflows (docs/**, lighthouserc.json, and the workflow file itself).
  • Do not run Lighthouse or Seaworthy on unrelated code-only pull requests: site-budget.yml and docs-doctor.yml do not start, and site-budget/docs-doctor in ci.yml only run on merge_group.

Never required on the pull request itself.

  • Full public corpus, mutation testing, Scorecard, scheduled fuzz, importers, source freshness.
  • Affected-ecosystem corpus (corpus.yml affected job) may run for signal; it stays non-required because it needs the network.

Concurrency. A newer push to the same pull request may cancel the older run.

Merge queue (30 minutes)

Goal. Everything a commit on main must have passed, on the exact merge result.

Runs.

  • The full code gate from the pull-request lane, including Windows — and the whole test suite, never the affected subset the pull-request lane runs.
  • macOS with Node 24 (check-cross-os), because that runner is scarce and belongs on the landing proof rather than every pull-request push. Its tarball hash joins the Linux and Windows records, so the merge-queue comparison covers all three runners.
  • Self-scan: fail on findings outside .offing-baseline.json.
  • Performance budget on the fixed fixture.
  • Package smoke (npm tarball, Docker image, local Action) when the lane still lists it on merge_group.
  • Site jobs (Lighthouse, Seaworthy, site budget, docs doctor) when the queued change touches site files; otherwise those jobs skip and ci-ok still passes. ci.yml calls site-budget.yml and docs-doctor.yml from merge_group because the queue ignores paths; changes.site decides.
  • ci-ok aggregates the above.

Rules.

  • Never cancel a merge_group run for a newer push.
  • The merge queue is the only path to main once #2029 is done; until then, treat a green queue run as the intended proof even if direct merges still exist.
  • Do not put corpus, mutation, or Scorecard into the queue budget.

Main (15 minutes)

Goal. After the merge queue is the only path, do not re-prove the same gate on every push.

Target (after #2029 and #2030).

  • Badge publish to the badges branch.
  • Pages deploy once per merge batch, not once per commit (#2031).
  • Any remaining release-branch Action bundle build the release chain still starts from main.
  • Do not cancel a main run that is the only verification left for a commit. Report cancelled share; keep it under 5%.

Until the queue is enforced. Keep the full ci.yml gate on push to main so history stays covered. That transitional cost is accepted; removing it is #2030's job after #2029.

Nightly and scheduled (60 minutes per workflow)

Goal. Signals that are too slow, too flaky, or too network-heavy for the merge path.

Work Workflow (today) Cadence (today)
Mutation testing mutation.yml Nightly
Parser fuzz (scheduled) fuzz.yml Nightly (+ optional PR path filter)
Package smoke (scheduled) package-smoke.yml Nightly
CI health / quarantine ci-health.yml Nightly + weekly
Full public corpus corpus.yml (full) Weekly
Record full corpus corpus.yml (record) Twice monthly
Scorecard + floor scorecard.yml, scorecard-floor.yml Weekly
CodeQL (scheduled scan) codeql.yml Weekly (also runs on every PR and main push)
Open alerts gate open-alerts.yml Push to main + daily
MCP listings mcp-listings.yml Weekly
Label sync labels.yml Weekly + path pushes

The scheduled runs must not be required status checks. A red nightly run opens follow-up work; it does not block a green queue. Affected, full, and record corpus runs live in one file (corpus.yml) with a mode input for workflow_dispatch.

Release (45 minutes)

Goal. One chain: verify → build → publish each channel → smoke. A failed stage is safe to rerun.

In scope.

  • Changelog notes and gates in RELEASING.md.
  • npm publish with provenance.
  • Action bundle on release/<tag> (not on main).
  • Standalone binaries, signatures, attestations.
  • Quickstart smoke against the published package.
  • Container and Homebrew channels the release docs list.

Stages. release.yml is a thin orchestrator that calls reusable stage workflows (verify, build, publish per channel including npm via the npm-publish job, smoke). A version tag runs the full chain in one workflow run so a failed stage is safe to re-run. A manual run with dry_run exercises every stage and publishes nothing. Those tasks keep this lane's budget and the rule that main does not carry the Action bundle.

Failure runbook

This section is the runbook for red CI: what each common failure looks like in the logs, why it happens, and what to do. It documents main as it is today; if a later task renames a step, update both the workflow and this page.

Start at ci-ok

ci-ok is the only required check, and its own log never explains the failure — it only says that a needed job failed or was cancelled:

::error::A job that ci-ok needs failed or was cancelled.

To find the real failure:

gh run list --workflow ci.yml --limit 10              # which runs went red
gh run view <run-id>                                  # job-by-job results
gh run view <run-id> --log-failed                     # only the failed steps' logs

--log-failed is the fastest path: every entry below is keyed to the step name it prints under. A cancelled result usually means a newer push cancelled an older pull-request run (allowed by the concurrency rule in the Pull request lane); that is not a failure to fix, and re-running the newest run is enough.

What actually fails (measured 2026-11-03)

366 workflow runs concluded failure in the 30 days up to the 2026-11-03 audit (earliest failure in the window: 2026-10-15). By workflow:

Workflow Failed runs Where this runbook covers it
CI 218 Entries below
corpus.yml (affected ecosystems) 51 Nightly and scheduled signal, not a gate
pages.yml (pages build and deployment) 42 Broken documentation site build
rules.yml (Rules (changed)) 14 Rule fixtures are missing or contradict the rule
workflow-lint.yml 13 Workflow lint runs after merge
Everything else (17 workflows, 28 runs) 28 Source freshness, site budget, mutation, package smoke, …

Re-derive the tally with (paging through the API because gh run list caps a single call):

gh api "repos/velella-sh/offing/actions/runs?per_page=100&status=failure&created=>2026-10-04" \
  --paginate --jq '.workflow_runs[] | [.name, .created_at] | @tsv'

Inside the CI workflow, 27 sampled failed runs in that window had these failing steps (a run counts once per failed step; ci-ok is the aggregate and appears in all 27):

Failing step Sampled runs
check job → npm run check 16
self-scan job → Scan this repository with the code under test 8
coverage job → Coverage diff for changed src files 5
check job → Dogfood Offing action 2
coverage job → Enforce coverage floors 1
check job → Guard the quality gate against main 1
check job → Audit dependencies (runtime, then the full lockfile) 1
seaworthy job → Run arminazimi/seaworthy@… 1

The sample covers the most recent failed CI runs at audit time, not all 218 — treat the percentages as direction, not a service-level figure.

A test fails inside npm run check

Symptom. The npm run check step ends with a line naming the failed pipeline step, for example:

test: node tools/run-tests.mjs exited 1

Above it, the failing test file and assertion. The Linux check job runs as two time-balanced shards per Node version (check (ubuntu-latest, node 24, shard 0) and so on); a shard number only says which runner found the failure — the same files run unsharded locally.

Cause. A genuine assertion failure in the suite, or a build/type error that makes the suite unrunnable.

Fix. Reproduce locally — the same pipeline runs with npm run check, and one file alone runs with npm run test -- dist/tests/<name>.test.js (the test script builds first). Fix the code or the test, not the threshold: npm run check runs everything the gate runs, and skipping, quarantining, or loosening is not a fix an author may make to get a merge.

Tests pass on retry (flaky)

Symptom. The run is green, but the step summary lists:

Failed once, then passed on a single retry:

Cause. tools/run-tests.mjs re-runs a failed test file once in CI and reports single-retry passes as flaky. Flakiness is real signal, not noise to swallow.

Fix. Open an issue naming the file, reproduce with the same command under load, and fix the test. The weekly ci-health run lists what has been flaky this week (node tools/run-tests.mjs --list-weekly-flaky). Only an open issue buys a test a quarantine entry in tests/quarantine.json; quarantined files are skipped on pull_request/merge_group and still run nightly via node tools/run-tests.mjs --quarantine-only. Details: TESTING.md — Quarantine and flaky tests.

Red on Windows only (check (windows-latest, node 24))

Symptom. Linux check jobs are green; the check-cross-os job's Windows matrix entry fails the same npm run check step.

Cause. Path separators, line endings, or case-sensitive filesystem assumptions that Linux and macOS do not see.

Fix. Run the failing test on Windows (a local Windows box or a throwaway branch). Watch out for core.autocrlf locally: CI forces git config --global core.autocrlf false because tests apply patches in temporary repositories, and a local true can hide or manufacture exactly this failure.

Coverage floors missed (Enforce coverage floors)

Symptom. The coverage job prints:

Coverage floors failed.
lines: 92.4% (floor 93) FAIL

The step prints one metric: percent (floor N) ok|FAIL row for every metric it checks. Floors live in package.json under coverageFloors (today 93 lines / 87 branches / 93 functions) and pull requests must meet the same floors as main.

Cause. New or changed src/ code the suite does not exercise. Coverage is collected once, in the unsharded coverage job (OFFING_CHECK_COVERAGE=1), so the report you are judged by is the one from node tools/run-tests.mjs with coverage on.

Fix. Add tests for the uncovered paths; reproduce with npm run test:coverage. Lowering a floor in package.json is not an author-side fix — floors are a repo-wide decision for maintainers, in a separate reviewed change.

Coverage fell against main (Coverage diff for changed src files)

Symptom. Either the changed files' per-file report (written by dist/tools/coverage-diff.js into the step summary), or a total dropping below main's:

branches is 86.9%, below main's 87.4%.

Or, when the report itself is missing:

::error::The coverage run did not write lcov.info; the per-file coverage diff cannot run.

Cause. The diff compares this run's lcov.info with the artifact from the latest successful main run and flags per-file regressions and totals below main's report (with a small rounding tolerance). The ::error:: line means the coverage run produced no lcov.info at all.

Fix. Cover the files you changed. If a genuinely dead path was removed and that moved a percentage, explain the numbers in the PR description and let review decide; do not edit floors.

Quality gate loosened (Guard the quality gate against main)

Symptom. The step (node dist/tools/check-quality.js --against origin/main) prints findings in the form:

gate: TARGETS.<limit>: limit loosened from <old> to <new>; the quality gate may only tighten against the base ref
gate: fileSize: src/<file>.ts: lines raised from <old> to <new>; the allowlist may only shrink against the base ref
gate: <section>: <key>: new allowlist entry; remove it or fix the debt instead of raising the gate

followed by quality gate: allowlist and TARGETS hold against origin/main only when everything holds.

Cause. The PR edits benchmarks/quality-allowlist.json or the checker's TARGETS table (in tools/check-quality.ts, which --against reads from both refs) in any way that relaxes a limit against origin/main — a raised ceiling, a later expiry, a new entry, or a loosened numeric target. The gate may only tighten.

Fix. Restore the committed values and fix the underlying debt. Allowlist changes that loosen limits are maintainer decisions and belong in their own change, not bundled into a feature PR. See QUALITY.md.

Dependency advisory (Audit dependencies (runtime, then the full lockfile))

Symptom. Either npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=low fails, or the checker reports:

moderate advisory 1234 is not allowlisted; update the dependency or add an entry with an owner and expiry

Cause. The runtime dependency tree must have no advisory at any level. The full lockfile may carry only the specific advisories listed in benchmarks/quality-allowlist.json; high and critical advisories always fail, allowlisted or not.

Fix. npm audit locally, bump or replace the dependency (npm install <pkg>@<version>; let npm touch package-lock.json, never hand-edit it). A dev-only moderate/low advisory that cannot be fixed yet needs an allowlist entry with an owner and expiry, added through its own PR.

Offing finds something new in its own repository

Symptom. Two steps can fail this way: Scan this repository with the code under test (the self-scan job, on merge queue and main) prints one ::error:: line per finding:

::error::<rule-id> <finding-id>: new finding not covered by .offing-baseline.json

and Dogfood Offing action (the check job, Linux shard 0) fails when the action under test scans the checkout and finds high-or-worse issues outside the baseline.

Cause. The change introduced a lifecycle-risk finding in this repository's own files that .offing-baseline.json does not cover — usually a dependency EOL bump or a risky pattern added to source or workflows.

Fix. Remove or fix the offending usage; that almost always means the change itself. Adding a baseline entry is a deliberate, separately reviewed change to .offing-baseline.json, not a way to silence a merge you dislike.

Merge markers built into main

Symptom. npm run check fails during the build with lines like:

error TS1185: Merge conflict marker encountered.

Cause. A conflict was resolved by keeping both sides and committed. The suite proves this cannot survive even one job; if it reached main, bisect to the merge commit.

Fix. Resolve properly, rebuild (npm run build), push. On main, this is a revert-and-remerge, not a follow-up patch.

Generated docs out of date

Symptom. One of the Check … against the registry steps (reference pages, Open Graph images, answer pages) or the buildability checks fails with lines like:

stale: docs/rules/<rule-id>.md
<file>: generated content differs
missing generated file

Cause. A registry change landed without regenerating the committed docs it drives.

Fix. Regenerate with the matching script from package.json — npm run build:reference, npm run build:og-images, npm run build:answer-pages — and commit the tracked outputs. Never hand-edit generated files, and never commit the ones .gitignore owns (docs/llms-full.txt, docs/sitemap.xml, docs/rules/index.md, docs/dashboard/data.json, docs/api/v1/; they are built at site-build time).

Missing decision record (decisions.yml)

Symptom. The Decisions check reports:

Public contract changed without a decision record:

followed by the changed paths.

Cause. The PR touches schemas/, src/sdk.ts, or src/mcp.ts — public contract surfaces — without adding a new record under docs/decisions/.

Fix. Write the decision record in this PR (see the existing numbering; one file per decision, status included). If you believe the change is not a contract change, say so on the PR and get the path filter adjusted through maintainers — do not rename files to dodge the filter.

Rule fixtures missing or contradicting (Rules (changed))

Symptom. The rules.yml job's Test the affected rule fixtures step prints, per rule:

Failed <rule-id> (@velella/ebb/registry/<file>.json)
  match: expected at least one finding for "<rule-id>"; got none.

or

  clean: expected no findings for "<rule-id>"; got 3.

or

  match: missing fixture: tests/fixtures/<rule-id>/match is not a directory. Create both tests/fixtures/<rule-id>/match and clean; see docs/RULES.md.

Cause. A rule's tests/fixtures/<rule-id>/match must report it and .../clean must not. The job runs the rules whose fixtures changed, and every rule with fixtures when the diff moves @velella/ebb to another version. A detector change that stops reporting a rule, or a new Ebb version whose rule no longer matches its fixture, fails here.

Fix. Correct the detector or the fixture directories; see RULES.md for the fixture contract. When the rule itself is wrong, fix it in Ebb. New fixtures are scaffolded with offing new-rule.

Workflow lint runs after merge (Workflow lint)

Symptom. A push-triggered Workflow lint run on main is red — actionlint findings from Lint the workflows with actionlint, or zizmor exiting 14 on Audit the workflows and the Action with zizmor.

Cause. workflow-lint.yml triggers on pushes to main and manually, not on pull requests, so a bad workflow edit first shows up after it landed.

Fix. Repair in a follow-up PR. Suppress a deliberate, explained pattern inline with # zizmor: ignore[rule] -- reason. Because this workflow is not part of ci-ok, its red does not block merges — but repeated red here means lint should move into the PR lane, which would update this page.

Broken documentation site build (pages build and deployment, docs doctor, docs job)

Symptom. The Build the documentation site step fails with a Mizzen error from mizzen build. Second-most-failing workflow in the 30-day window above.

Cause. Bad front matter, a redirect that collides with a page, or a docs source the site build cannot process. The docs-only path of ci.yml builds the same site, so this usually also fails pre-merge — unless the breaking change reached main through another path. A red docs doctor run means the same thing: the doctor's own findings are report-only (level: none), so only the site build can turn it red.

Fix. Reproduce with npx @velella/mizzen check docs (plus --theme @velella/lateen) and fix the docs source. Mizzen config and theme changes belong in site-focused PRs.

Seaworthy fails on the built site (seaworthy job)

Symptom. The Run arminazimi/seaworthy@… step in pages.yml fails on the deployed-site checks.

Cause. A site change broke navigation, links, or the crawl expectations Seaworthy encodes.

Fix. Reproduce against the built site locally if possible; otherwise the pages.yml run's artifact (docs-site) is the thing to inspect. Seaworthy is not part of ci-ok, so this is a follow-up-work signal, not a merge blocker.

Site budget exceeded (Site budget)

Symptom. Measure the pages against the budgets (@lhci/cli autorun --config=lighthouserc.json) reports assertion failures such as:

largest-contentful-paint failure for maxNumericValue assertion.

with budgets: LCP 2500 ms, total page weight 163840 bytes, document size 40960 bytes.

Cause. A docs page grew past its Lighthouse budget — heavy inline content, new scripts, or images.

Fix. Slim the page (split content, drop weight). Editing lighthouserc.json to move a budget is a maintainer decision like any other gate loosening. In the merge queue the site-budget job is part of ci-ok, so the queue will not land a site change that exceeds a budget.

main is red

Symptom. An issue titled "main is red: CI is failing" with label area: devops exists and accumulates updates.

Cause. ci-health.yml watches every failed CI push run on main (via workflow_run) and maintains exactly one such issue. It closes itself once main's CI goes green.

Fix. Triage from the issue's body: it lists the failing runs and steps. Treat a red main as top priority — every later merge queue inherits the doubt. Do not open a second red-main issue by hand, and do not re-run the failing main commit hoping for green; fix forward or revert.

Nightly and scheduled signal, not a gate

Red corpus.yml (affected, full, or record), mutation.yml, scorecard.yml, scheduled CodeQL, or MCP-listing runs never block a green queue — see the Nightly lane and What this design deliberately leaves out. The affected-corpus job was the second-heaviest failure source in the 30-day window above; it needs the network, so its red is signal rather than a merge blocker, and what it means (upstream flakiness vs a detector regression) has to be read from the job log, not assumed. A red nightly run opens follow-up work (an issue) rather than blocking a merge; a repeatedly red nightly source is itself a bug worth filing. Full-corpus validation lives in VALIDATION.md; warm the corpus fixtures locally with npm run corpus:warm and check the tracked repositories with npm run validate:public-repos.

Release chain

Symptom. A release.yml run on a v* tag fails in one of its stages; publish.yml never runs on its own (workflow_call from release.yml only; it runs package smoke and the MCP Registry after the npm-publish job).

Cause. Verify, build, per-channel publish (npm, binaries, container, Homebrew, data bundle), or smoke failed. Stages receive the audited release_sha (since #2340), so a mid-chain failure cannot silently publish a newer commit.

Fix. The chain is designed so a failed stage is safe to re-run: gh run rerun <run-id> --failed resumes from the failed stage. Read RELEASING.md before retrying anything that publishes; a manual dry_run run exercises every stage and publishes nothing. Whether a specific published channel completed is not measurable from the runbook — check the run's stage logs.

What this design deliberately leaves out of the merge gate

  • Network corpus validation.
  • Mutation score (gated separately per QUALITY.md once measured).
  • OpenSSF Scorecard floor (scheduled alert until the score meets the quality target).
  • Marketplace-only publish steps.

Workflow inventory

Every file under .github/workflows/ belongs to a lane above and has a stated purpose. Owner for all of them is @arminazimi (.github/CODEOWNERS /.github/workflows/). Count after #2025: 33 files (corpus-pr.yml and corpus-record.yml folded into corpus.yml).

A last-run audit on 2026-11-03 found no unused workflows to delete. Empty run history is expected for offing-reusable.yml (only workflow_call, runs in caller repositories) and for scorecard-floor.yml (added 2026-11-02; first cron is Saturday). Do not delete a workflow here just because a later task will fold it.

File Lane Trigger Purpose
ci.yml Pull request / merge queue / main pull_request, push to main, merge_group Main gate: classify docs vs code, npm run check matrix, quality, self-scan path, and the required ci-ok aggregator
decisions.yml Pull request pull_request on contract paths Fail when a public-contract change lacks a decision record
rules.yml Pull request / main pull_request / push on fixture paths and package-lock.json Fixture-test the rules the diff can affect
docs-doctor.yml Pull request / merge queue pull_request on docs site paths; workflow_call from ci.yml; workflow_dispatch mizzen check on the documentation site (errors fail; warnings are reported)
site-budget.yml Pull request / merge queue pull_request on site paths; workflow_call from ci.yml; workflow_dispatch Fail when the docs site exceeds size or LCP budgets
fuzz.yml Pull request / nightly pull_request on parser paths; nightly schedule; workflow_dispatch Deeper parser fuzz than the tight budget inside npm run check
workflow-lint.yml Main push to main on workflow paths; workflow_dispatch actionlint + zizmor on workflow YAML and action.yml
pages.yml Main push to main; workflow_dispatch Build the docs site, Seaworthy + Lighthouse, deploy to GitHub Pages
labels.yml Main / nightly pull_request / push on label paths; weekly schedule; workflow_dispatch Sync .github/labels.yml and check good-first-issue briefs
release.yml Main / release push to main; version v* tags; workflow_dispatch One release chain: Action bundle on release/<tag>, npm via the npm-publish job, binaries, provenance, channels, smoke
package-smoke.yml Merge queue / nightly merge_group; nightly schedule; workflow_dispatch Prove npm tarball, Docker image, and local Action scan the same fixture
ci-health.yml Nightly workflow_run of CI on main; schedules; workflow_dispatch Open/close devops issues on main failures, measure CI duration, quarantine flaky tests
mutation.yml Nightly Nightly schedule; workflow_dispatch Mutation testing matrix (too slow for the merge gate)
corpus.yml Pull request / main / nightly pull_request / push on detector paths; weekly + twice-monthly schedules; workflow_dispatch with mode (affected / full / record) Affected-ecosystem signal; full public corpus validate in eight shards plus a merge job; recorded full-run PR
scorecard.yml Nightly Weekly schedule; branch_protection_rule; workflow_dispatch OpenSSF Scorecard publish + SARIF upload
scorecard-floor.yml Nightly Weekly schedule (after Scorecard); workflow_dispatch Alert when the published Scorecard score is below the QUALITY.md floor
codeql.yml Pull request / main / nightly Every pull_request; push to main; weekly schedule; workflow_dispatch CodeQL analysis of every proposed change and main
open-alerts.yml Push to main Push to main; daily schedule; workflow_dispatch Fail on any open code-scanning or Dependabot alert on main that tools/open-alerts-baseline.json does not accept
mcp-listings.yml Nightly Weekly schedule; workflow_dispatch Compare tracked MCP directory listings to server.json
publish.yml Release workflow_call from release.yml package smoke and MCP Registry (the npm publish itself is in release.yml)
gitlab-sync.yml Release v* tags; workflow_dispatch Push the release commit and tags to the GitLab CI/CD Catalog project
offing-reusable.yml Product (caller) workflow_call only Reusable per-repository Offing scan for other repositories to uses:
org-scan.yml Product (caller) workflow_call; workflow_dispatch Organization-wide scan, rollup, and optional Slack/Teams digest

Last-run audit (2026-11-03)

Checked with gh run list --workflow <file> --limit 1 against velella-sh/offing. Since then sources.yml, importers.yml, and data-release.yml have moved to Ebb with the lifecycle data.

Outcome Workflows
Ran successfully within about a week ci.yml, ci-health.yml, codeql.yml, corpus.yml, decisions.yml, docs-doctor.yml, fuzz.yml, gitlab-sync.yml, labels.yml, mcp-listings.yml, package-smoke.yml, pages.yml, publish.yml, release.yml, rules.yml, scorecard.yml, site-budget.yml, workflow-lint.yml
Ran (failed — still active signal, not unused) mutation.yml (nightly), sources.yml (nightly), org-scan.yml (manual/product path)
Older success, still on its trigger data-release.yml (last data-v* / release-related push 2026-10-21), importers.yml (last schedule 2026-10-27)
No runs in this repository (expected) offing-reusable.yml (workflow_call only), scorecard-floor.yml (first Saturday cron not yet due)

Changing this page

  • Accepted design. After decision 0024 is accepted, workflow pull requests that move work between lanes or raise a budget update this page in the same change.
  • Inventory. When you add, rename, delete, or change the purpose of a workflow file, update the Workflow inventory table in the same pull request.
  • Workflow changes. A pull request that edits .github/workflows/ fills in the pull request template section and keeps the runner-minute ceiling at or below the budget.
  • Shared setup. Checkout-independent Node install and cache move into one composite action in #2026; lanes above stay the same.
